whatever they did with the remaster created so many glitches and bs that its almost becoming unplayable..

the quest system is broken, the navigation is broken, the witcher senses are worse compared to the previous versions... i hope they did not vibe code the remastered version

This review is for the remaster, not the original game.

While the original game is an unparalleled masterpiece the remaster is a huge downgrade. Graphics wise it looks far worse in many moments. Especially the well crafted lightning that contributed to atmosphere is far worse with the remaster. It looks awfull with ray tracing and path tracing. And just a bit worse without them. Path tracing is more of a poorly done tech demo than a good graphical upgrade.

Some textures look a tad nicer and higher detailed.
However for the slight increase in graphics quality if you disregard the lightning a high end pc is now required. This is a serious regression compared to the old version.

UI management has been slightly improved. One of the few positives.

Monster AI is very buggy now. The run atop of each other, randomly deaggro mid fight and are very easy to cheese. Geralt also plays far worse in combat and just randomly focuses thin air. Luckily you can turn on a slide to get closer to the old behavior. So the combat as core part of the game is far far worse. Most challenging encounter are now completely trivial due to buggy monster AI. It reduces the game mostly to a visual novel with buggy fights as trivial filler content.

Sometimes the minimap buggs out and shows like 50+ quest markers as your currently tracked quest.

Visual clarity is far worse. If you cast yrden you have no clue where it starts and end depending on the terrain.

New skilltree looks pretty mid. Nothing really interesting there. Signs seem to be completely overpowered as well.

There are also new bugs that prevent progression in some quests.

Overall you can see that this remaster was done by a contractor that was paid for it and not a labour of love by people who cared about the final product, unlike the original game.

Original game was a 10/10.
Remaster is 4/10 because it was build on good foundations. As standalone it would be pretty poor 2/10,

Edit: After playing for a while it gets even worse. …

I have completed the game twice before, once before the next-gen update, so I do not question the core games merit. claims.claim: Reviewers praise the game's detailed open-world exploration, world building, atmospheric locations, and musical score.

citations.review_text:
I love this game to the core, three best things that I love in the game are,

CD Projekt Red created an incredibly atmospheric, living world. Every village, swamp, and city feels authentic, dangerous, and deeply immersive to explore. while playing it feels like I am inside their world. 

The combat system is fantastic. It strikes the perfect balance between preparation and action, letting you deeply customize your build—like turning Geralt into a heavy-armor, heavy-hitting juggernaut. Reading the Bestiary before going to every fight against a monster make me feel like I am going to a fight, experience was very good and immersive. Massive gears and build sets available and we as a player can customize according to our play style.

The soundtrack is a masterpiece. The intense, folk-inspired combat music and atmospheric exploration tracks completely elevate the mood of the entire game. Silver for Monsters all time fav. If a pleasant music changes to a terrific intense one get ready to shit.

This is my first time playing The Witcher 3; I haven't played the first or second games. I initially bought just the base game for $2 and wow, what a time to start playing for the first time! Right while I was in the middle of my playthrough, CD Projekt Red went ahead and gave away the Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine DLCs for free 👍 The Next Gen update is pretty good, and the Remastered version is even better in terms of lighting, gameplay, UI, and more. It’s the perfect time for me to play this for the first time. I feel like I got this game for free.

This is one of the best open world games I have played. The map is very detailed, the forest is very dense with trees and bushes. the atmosphere felt very lively. The map is huge, and every location is beautiful. It’s very relaxing to explore on horseback with Roach, even though there are enemies and monsters along the way. One of the games with the best soundtracks I’ve ever heard; the music fits perfectly with the locations you find yourself in. 

I’ve finished the story, and what a game. I could have finished it faster in under 40 hours but that’s because I spent time on side quests, free roaming, and even replaying parts of the game after hitting a few "bad endings." 

It was very emotional at the end, with plenty of ups and downs throughout the game; fortunately, I managed to get the good ending. To be honest, I did follow some guides to ensure I got that outcome, But I didn't care I just wanted to get the good ending I desired, and it paid off.

The side quests here are deep and substantial; some are fun, while others are not.

and here's what I don't like: 
1. You have to really understand the choice of dialogue because it affects the story. Also it could be a trap, and repeating it would set you back quite a bit.
2. The monsters here are  annoying especially in caves, underground etc. they are quite strong if your strength is still lacking.
3. Scary characters, creepy monsters? And the music is that also m…

One of the best games ever made, even years later

Honestly, The Witcher 3 is one of those games that reminds you why you love gaming in the first place. Even after all these years, it still feels special, and playing it on PC with the remastered/next-gen update makes the experience even better.

The world is absolutely incredible. You can spend hours just exploring, hunting monsters, stumbling across random quests, or getting distracted by something completely unrelated to what you originally planned to do. And somehow, even the smallest side quests have more interesting stories than the main plot of many other games.

Geralt is such a great character, and the writing is easily one of the biggest strengths of the game. The characters feel real, the choices actually make you think, and the world isn't just black and white. Sometimes there is no perfect answer, and that's what makes everything so memorable.

On PC, the game looks fantastic, especially with the next-gen improvements. The atmosphere, the landscapes, the sunsets, the music... everything comes together beautifully. Riding through Velen, exploring Novigrad, or getting lost in Toussaint never gets old.

What I appreciate most is that this game respects your intelligence. It doesn't need to constantly hold your hand or throw meaningless activities at you just to make the world feel bigger. Almost everything has a purpose, a story, or something interesting behind it.

I'm 35, and I've played plenty of games over the years, but The Witcher 3 is still one of those rare experiences that stays with you long after you finish it. It's not just about combat or graphics. It's about the characters, the atmosphere, the choices, and the feeling of being part of a genuinely living world.

CD Projekt Red absolutely nailed it with this one. If you've never played it, you're missing out on something special. And if you've already played it, it's absolutely worth coming back to.

An easy 10/10 for me. A true…

Was recommended by a coworker as we were talking about our favorite story games, and lets just say I was hooked immediately. The characters are all well developed with many choices resulting in varying outcomes and I would easily put it in my top 5 as of this moment (I haven't even fully completed the main quest line ~70hrs in). 


Ps. Tris and Yen please take me back, it was a mistake I swear :(

Absolutely GOAT'ed, every sidequest, collectible and even contracts feel just as good as any story mission, also received the remastered version and DLC's for free. Definetly worth the time, seeing the characters and getting choices that affect the world and story. If you need some time to drift away and adventure in another world this is one of the best options for that!

An absolute masterpiece. I finally understand why this game is considered one of the greatest games of all time. The world is incredibly immersive, lore is insanely deep, the characters are unforgettable, and the writing is phenomenal, with side quests that are more compelling than some games’ entire main stories. One moment you’re laughing at Geralt’s dry humor, the next you’re questioning your own decisions or getting emotionally wrecked by a quest you thought was just another monster contract. Everything feels alive, and even the smallest stories feel meaningful. Add an incredible soundtrack, satisfying combat, and a world that makes you want to get lost in it for hours, and you have something truly special. This game has officially become my new favorite. What a journey.

claims.claim: Reviewers point out various tedious mechanics, such as inventory management, weight limits, item crafting ingredients, and vendor currency limits.

citations.review_text:
What a great game. What a memorable journey. What a remarkable experience.

I am definitely not a fan of RPGs, and this was the first one I have played through. While it definitely has a lot of things that I do not like or enjoy, it has ten times more things I love and can’t get enough of. 

Let me start with the negatives. This game has so much unnecessary bloat that my eyes just rolled. +2% chance to cause bleeding or +3% resistance to slash damage? Who cares about such insignificant stats in a singleplayer game? Hundreds of types of crafting ingredients. Completely unnecessary mechanics, such as vendors always having very little money to buy your junk, so you sell few things, then meditate for five days so their budget restores and you can sell more. Or, almost always, you have to return to the quest's original assigner so he can tell you, “thanks for letting me know, here is your reward”. Things that are supposed to feel more realistic just add more grind and repetitiveness and feel like a chore. But those things are very typical for RPGs, so thank god that it is not required to embrace them, especially on lower difficulties or with some accessibility options turned on. Kudos for that.

But the positives highly outweigh the negatives. With the remastered version and path tracing turned on, this game has jaw dropping visuals. Lighting is perfect in almost all scenarios. World design is truly realistic - city design, foliage, and character density feel truly authentic. Combat is really great and offers a huge variety of options. Side quests and contracts offer a lot and bring a lot of value to the overall package. The main storyline is great and engaging, delivering a lot of memorable moments. But I did not enjoy it as much as I could simply because it relies a lot on the expectation that you have played previous entries, which I have not. I understand that it is a third entry into a series, but I think higher emphasis could be given to introducing characters to n…

250 hours later, I completed the Remastered with all DLCs. I still need to upgrade the majority of my Witcher School Gear to Grandmaster in preparation for Songs of the Past. 
While I have enjoyed my 2nd playthrough after a decade, there are is significant amount of bugs I'm surprised remains after all this time.

Most notably, I could not complete the "Collect 'Em All" achievement without enabling the in-game console, which is exclusive to PC players and required editing game files. Zoltan's Gwent Card, which can be won either during the Gwent Tutorial at the Start of the Game or below a Hanged Man's body later on if you missed it (which was my case), never spawned. I thoroughly researched my issue online and found dozens of online posts describing the exact same issue, both from the original and Remastered Game. Ultimately, I had to manually add the card to my inventory via the in-game console, which finally completed the Side Quest for me after 200h+ of playtime.

Eredin Commander of the Red Riders, which is a Leader Card of the Monster Gwent Faction, is permanently locked and unplayable both while checking your Gwent Decks or playing a Match, despite the game registering all Gwent Cards collected, the "Collect Em' All" achievement being completed, and the related merchant usually selling the card no longer selling it.

I have experience numerous crashes during my playthrough from basic interactions such as Fast Traveling to a different region, looting chests or selling items at Merchants.

**8.5/10**

I'm not usually a fan of open-world games, but I had a genuinely great time with The Witcher 3. The storytelling, writing, and soundtrack are all top-tier. My biggest criticism is the combat, which started to feel repetitive and underwhelming as the game progressed.

Despite that, it was an incredible experience, and I'm really looking forward to the next Witcher game and the third expansion!

This game does NOT hold up to nostalgia. This plays like modern AAA slop. The combat is boring and repetitive, the sword breaks every 5 hits, the cutscenes are long and boring, and the quest gameplay is just following the quest marker (or at best follow the red line in the quest area). At least the graphics look nice.

Also, I've noticed- and it's started to bother me- that Geralt talks like a disinterested 14 year old trying to sound like a tough guy.  He's always like "Ugh, I guess I'll help... but I won't like it."

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight that side quests are exceptionally well written and offer engaging stories comparable to main campaigns.

citations.review_text:
Honestly it took me three tries to get into this game
My first playthrough I found the combat janky and the story didn't interest me enough so I gave up after just a few hours in
On my second I managed to stick it out until I finished the first area, but even then it wasn't really maintaining my interest

However, on my third playthrough (after the remaster) I finally understood what made this game so special.
First of all, the story was one of the best in any game I had ever played and kept my complete attention the entire way through
Second, I finally understood the combat. Scouring the map to find the hidden locations and crafting recipes revealed a surprisingly deep combat system that weaved together simple things like choosing the best weapons, armour and magic with actual preparation and builds that made the game even more immersive.
Third the side content was exceptional. It's a common praise for the Witcher 3 but many of the side quests were so well written that they could easily be the main quests in their own games; also, once I understood gwent it was probably the most fun mini-game I had ever played
Finally, the dlc was just as good as the main game and introduced enough new content to keep me gripped even after I finished the main story

⭐ THE WITCHER 3: WILD HUNT — A MASTERPIECE THAT WILL STAY WITH ME FOREVER

Some games are fun. Some games are unforgettable. And then there's The Witcher 3.

I went into this game expecting a fantasy RPG, but I came out feeling like I'd lived an entire lifetime in another world.

The world of The Witcher 3 is something else. Every village, every forest, every tavern, every little conversation feels alive. You don't just follow a story here; you become a part of it. And Geralt? What a character. A man who pretends not to care, yet somehow ends up carrying the weight of everyone else's problems. His dry humour, his personality, his relationships, and those little moments of humanity make him one of the greatest protagonists in gaming history.

The side quests deserve a special mention. I've played games where side quests feel like chores, but here, even a random contract can turn into a memorable story. Sometimes you start a quest expecting to kill a monster and end up questioning humanity, morality, and your own decisions.

And the soundtrack? Absolutely beautiful. Riding through Velen, exploring Novigrad, or simply wandering around Toussaint while the music plays in the background... pure magic.

But what makes this game truly special is that it makes you care. Your choices have consequences, characters leave an impression, and certain moments stay in your mind long after you've turned off your PC.

I don't know how many games will make me feel this way again, but I know one thing:

**I'd give anything to experience The Witcher 3 for the first time all over again.**

10/10? No. That's not enough.

This isn't just a game. It's an experience, a journey, and a world I wasn't ready to leave.

Geralt of Rivia, you magnificent bastard. ❤️

🐺 Wind's howling... and I think I'll stay a little longer.

claims.claim: Reviewers praise the game's expansive open world and atmosphere.

citations.review_text: A very large world that feels alive, with no shortage of meaningful content. The main narrative is solid, and the expansions are fully realized. With the developers continuously supporting the game, it's hard not to recommend The Witcher 3 to anyone looking for an unforgettable single-player experience.

The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt complete edition goes on sale for very little every now and then. I would definitely recommend buying it on sale and, to be honest, it is even worth the full price.

I have never been this fond of an open world RPG. The world of Witcher 3 feels incredibly lively and vibrant even 11 years after its release. The architecture, soundtrack, characters, dialogue and everything else in this game create a somewhat warm atmosphere that keeps you hooked.

The main story which, of course, includes our favorite sarcastic white wolf, Geralt of Rivia, is quite well written. The choices you make actually affect the story throughout the whole game, not just the ending. The main story takes place in many different locations which all feel unique and aren't just copied and pasted. And even if you were to only play the main story, you would still get your money's worth because, at least for me, the main story itself took me a good 50 hours to complete.

Then there are the DLCs. Hearts of Stone felt like a fun little adventure in the map you've already gotten used to. It also added a bunch of new features to the base game. Blood and Wine, on the other hand, introduced a completely new area to the game! Toussaint and the new faces it brings feel fresh after the base game and HoS. It almost feels like a completely new game.

All in all, I would recommend The Witcher 3 to anyone. Yes, to anyone. You can't go wrong with this game. It will hook you in and keep you hooked for hours.

Graphic is great as well they improved it with this remastered since when first played it (before i dropped it) i played the original (or next-gen?) version of this game and the improvement really showed especially lighting and camera angle also improved

Overall its a Very Good game.
It got some bugs sure like sometimes when i killed an enemy while they are knocked  down they would like stand up and just stand there idly but it didnt really ruin the game or anything  at all.

Highly recommend for people who liked RPG with Dialog that have Consequences and a really engaging and good story! 
I rate it 9/10

Phenomenal. Absolutely phenomenal. Side quests are (often) just as involved as main quests and never feel like a waste of time. Characters and story are exceptionally written. Many choices do have consequences, instead of the disappointing standard of "Yes", "no", "Yes, and I hate you" all leading to the same outcome. I'm confident in saying this game exceeded all my expectations!

single_points.text: One reviewer says that enabling ray tracing or path tracing brings their PC to its knees and drastically reduces framerates.

citation.review_text:
A beautiful game made even more beautiful.

True to CDPR tradition it once again brings some PCs to their knees. My vintage 2070 Super ran the next gen version beautifully, but now if I desire to admire the game in full beauty with ray tracing and path tracing I'd be lucky to get 40 fps with frame gen (and 12 fps without it). Still, ray tracing alone with no path tracing already transforms how the foliage and world interacts with light and shadow (and dare I say sometimes the game looks even better in that half-way state, path tracing can sometimes 'ruin' the cinematic-ness here and there) and brings it up to a very playable 70-80 fps with FSR framegen.

Some visual pitfalls of earlier versions are unfortunately still there - a darker nights mod (especially paired with a mod for torches you can hold while riding a horse or fighting) is still essential to the experience in my opinion, the vanilla nights are just so bright. I hoped a new lighting system would make that not be the case, but oh well.

Also no change this big happens without some new bugs. Cave interiors will often become weirdly pale-ly lit with ray tracing on. Sometimes grass will just straight up not exist for the first minute or so since loading a save.
An especially annoying bug I encountered: if you load an older save, the game will notify you about your skills points getting reset because of the reworked system. You assign the refunded points again and then decide to start a New Game+ based on that save. As soon as you get into gameplay you get the same notification again about the changed system, which once again forcibly completely resets your already rebuilt skill tree - and that reset is a completely separate one from the normal voluntary NG+ ability of resetting your skill tree. A frustrating start to a new save - instead of stepping out on the balcony to admire the upgraded view you instead get frustrated.
But still, those are minor issues that don't detract from the beauty and atmosphere of…
